cur-fossil-kap-kobenhavn.dateNote: In 2022 Kurt Kjær and Eske Willerslev's team read DNA from mud in this formation in Peary Land, in the far north of Greenland. At about 2 million years old (Early Pleistocene) it was the oldest DNA known. It shows a forest with mastodons, reindeer, hares and geese.
cur-fossil-kap-kobenhavn.summary: Greenland mud with 2-million-year-old DNA from a lost Arctic forest with mastodons.
